notes_for_editor: Only tower-specific source is the tnlandforms index (page revised 2016, one compiler). The index says names for towers 73 and above are its author's own, so 'Oliver' is a label, not verified as the tower's name. The index gives the elevation (159) with no unit; the story reads it as feet, which fits the rest of the list but is not stated. The index row carries the annotation 'topo army'; I found no key for that code, so I did not interpret it. No source found on build date, staffing, fire history, fate or present condition. Story body is about 130 words and rests on one index source, so consider holding for editor review. Neither register lists a Georgia tower called Oliver (checked the full NHLR Georgia list of 29 and the FFLOS Georgia list of 2; both lists are now quoted in evidence). Evans County's Wikipedia page mentions a community called Camp Oliver (with the Glisson Store), a possible naming lead that I did not verify or cite. Do not confuse with Oliver, Georgia, a different community in Screven County. The elevation of 159 is read as feet (48.5 m). Coordinates were not checked against any map.
